resources.string: Sample copied text for the tutorial
With an empty field, the third cell shows the last thing you copied. Tap it to paste.
Swipe down (or long-press) on the third cell to open the clipboard history.
Tap the trash icon on an entry to remove it from the history.
If the keyboard corrects something you did not want, delete right after: your word comes back and it will not be corrected again. Try it and continue.
After a space, the centre may offer the word that usually comes next. Tap it to accept.
Swipe a suggestion right (green) to save it to your personal dictionary, or left (red) to ban and purge it.
Take the tutorial by tapping here
To predict the next word, the keyboard stores locally which words you type after which. Everything stays on-device and is never sent anywhere; you can disable it at any time.
When deleting right after an autocorrection, undo it and restore what you had typed
The corrector reads the text you type to offer suggestions. Everything is processed on-device: nothing is sent anywhere or logged (unlike bigrams).
Set colors, height and languages to your liking, then tap Continue.
Tap only center letters to type: %1$s.
Swipe from the center of a key toward a corner letter to type it.
Now type the whole phrase: \"Who wants kiwi and chocolate?\".
Type any sentence, as you normally would.
Swipe left over the space to erase.
Swipe right over the space to redo.
Hold your finger at the left edge to erase continuously.
Swipe up twice over the space to enable caps lock.
Swipe up once to disable caps lock.
Drag the round knob to the end of the second paragraph.
Swipe down over the space to insert a line break.
Tap the round knob once to open the numbers.
Tap a number to type it.
Swipe the strip to change page and tap @.
Tap the round knob twice to open the symbol layer.
Tap abc to close the symbol layer.
Tap the capsule to switch language, then again to return to yours.
Explore the cards: each opens a settings section. When ready, tap Finish.

string-array.name: section_explains
string-array.item: Here you choose which languages cycle on the keyboard and the UI language.
Here you customize the keyboard and app colors (dark and light).
Here you adjust height, grid gap, space bar and margins.
Here you tune thresholds and sensitivities for gestures, cursor and erase.
Here you enable or disable comforts like auto-cap or auto-space.
Here you control which animations play and how fast.
Here you manage the bigram log (privacy) and advanced options.
Here you find the tutorial again and the GitHub link to report bugs.

resources.string: The tutorial (and the keyboard) need you to enable ThumbGridTest in the system keyboard settings. Do it and come back here to continue; the tutorial will unlock itself.
Tria el teu idioma / Elige tu idioma / Choose your language
Log bigrams to optimize the layout
Enter your pattern, PIN or password to view the bigram log
Changes apply the next time the keyboard is shown.

A local file will be created on the device collecting the letter pairs you type, so the keyboard layout can be optimized. It contains no passwords or sensitive fields, never leaves the device or goes to the cloud, and you can delete it at any time.
The repository is not published yet. Once it is, this button will take you straight to it.
You can tweak the sensitivity of several things in the Sensitivity section of the settings; no need to go one by one explaining the units.

string-array.name: tutorial_text
string-array.item: This is a sample text for the tutorial. You don\'t need to read it: it\'s here so you can try the keyboard\'s functions.
This text is exclusive to the tutorial. It lets you try every function on both small segments and a whole paragraph.
As you can see, everything is split into small parts. That\'s so it\'s easier to remember which sentence you are erasing or redoing, though it won\'t matter in the sliding section.
If you\'re reading this, you\'ve gone further than expected. Most people give up at the second paragraph and start sliding to erase everything, which is exactly what we wanted you to do.

This last paragraph is deliberately long so you can try continuous erase by holding your finger at the left edge, and so redo has plenty of work coming back. If you erased and redid all of this without getting lost, you already have more control over the keyboard than most users will ever have, and you didn\'t even have to read a real manual.
P.S.: Did you actually read it all, or just skim the end? If you read it all, congratulations: you\'re in the 0.1% of users who read sample texts. The keyboard and I are very proud of you.

string-array.name: tutorial_descs
string-array.item: Before starting, make the keyboard yours: colors (dark and light), height, gap, bottom margin and capsule languages.
Tap the center letters of each key to type them. Type the word CASA using only center letters.

Corner letters are typed by swiping from the center toward their direction. Type the phrase \"Who wants kiwi and chocolate?\" (the tutorial will verify it). Once you have it, feel free to try other gestures on any letter.
Now type any sentence as if nothing. You usually won\'t need gestures: the keyboard is fast even tapping only big letters.
Swipe left on the space bar to erase. Erase at least two short sentences of the text.
Swipe right on the space bar to redo. Recover at least as much as you erased.
With an empty field, the third cell of the strip shows the last thing you copied. One tap pastes it as-is, without opening menus or switching apps.
Swiping down (or long-pressing) on the third cell opens the recent clipboard history. Each entry has a trash icon to remove it, and entries expire on their own after one hour unused.
When the keyboard corrects a word you did not want, delete right after the correction: you get your original text back and the keyboard remembers not to correct it again.
If you enable prediction in settings, the keyboard learns which words you type after which and offers the next one with an empty field. Everything stays on-device.
Swipe a suggestion right (green) to save the word to your personal dictionary, or left (red) to ban it and purge it from learning. It is the management gesture: fast and without holding your finger.
Hold your finger at the left edge while sliding to erase continuously. Empty the long paragraph.
Two quick up-swipes enable caps lock: type three capitals and disable it with another up-swipe.
Drag the round knob to move the cursor to the end of the second paragraph, then swipe down on space to insert a line break.
One tap on the round knob opens numbers: type a digit, slide the strip to see more pages and insert the @ from the second one.
Two taps on the round knob open the symbol layer: insert a symbol like € or © and close it by tapping abc.
Tap the language capsule (bottom left) to switch language, then tap again until you\'re back to yours.
Each card below is one settings section. Once the repository is public, the button will take you to GitHub to report bugs.
